### feature-loop.sh: lower the default memory cap from 4G to 3.5G

change `kuyulwnwzxxu` · [log `2e15450dbbf2`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/6751f657-78ac-484c-8e36-eef607a6c325/2e15450dbbf2bcc0838a091dae54ec42c4f50d0d4964157673a3e399495a0cbf.jsonl.gz)

Proofs and model checks now run in the verification pipeline, so the loop's scope only holds the Claude session and inline builds. Measured in capped systemd scopes with swap off: cargo build --release peaks at 1.1G, cargo test at 1.7G (finishes under a 1.5G cap), sync.py check --full at 0.85G, and the full Box Office Gradle build at 1.9G (killed at 1.5G, finishes at 2G). With the Claude process on top, 3.5G leaves about 1 GB of headroom for the heaviest case. README updated to match; FEATURE_LOOP_MEMORY_MAX still overrides it.

### 1. 2026-11-04 05:08 UTC

> Let's review the FEATURE_LOOP_MEMORY_MAX setting -- previously it was set to 4G because that loop ran calculations. Now those are offloaded to the run-verification loop. What can we reduce this memory setting to? Is 2G safe?

**Reply:**

**No, 2G isn't safe. 3G is the lowest cap I'd use.**

The main job did move to the verification pipeline, but the loop still builds and tests inline, and one of those builds needs most of 2 GB by itself. I ran each one in its own systemd scope, as the loop does, and measured peak memory. That figure includes page cache, which the system can reclaim, so the real test was whether each run finishes under a hard cap with swap off:

| Work run inside the loop | Peak, no cap | Under a cap |
|---|---|---|
| `cargo build --release` (lib, LTO) | 1.1G | finishes at 1.5G |
| `cargo test` (lib) | 1.7G | finishes at 1.5G (cache reclaimed) |
| `sync.py check --full` (run on every commit) | 0.85G | finishes at 1G |
| Box Office `gradlew build` (all modules, no system tests) | 1.9G | **killed for lack of memory at 1.5G**, finishes at 2G |

The Claude process runs in the same scope and adds about 300 MB now, more as a session gets long. The Gradle daemon also stays in the scope between turns unless it's stopped.

A full Gradle build plus Claude comes to about 2.2–2.5 GB, so a 2G cap would kill builds in the `spring` loop, which works on Box Office. The other loops (`tla`, `relational`, `features`) only use cargo and `sync.py`, and those would fit in 2G but with little margin. Under 3G every case passes with about 0.5–1 GB to spare.
